title: Quant fidelity inspector with synthetic challenge cohorts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an automated validation harness that builds small, interpretable cohorts of prompts (including synthetic adversarial variants) to exercise FP8/INT8 calibration and quantization profiles. The harness should run as part of the quant rollout pipeline and produce per-cohort fidelity summaries, a cohort-stability score, and a deterministic pass/fail gate that can be consumed by rollouts and CI. This ticket covers the harness service, cohort generators, metric computation, integration with the calibration runner, and an initial set of user-facing failure signals for the console and alerting.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can generate 5 canonical cohorts for any given model: anchor, conversational-context, long-seq, numeric-stress, and synthetic-adversarial.

For a sample of 1k queries across cohorts, harness computes and stores: token-level perplexity delta, top-1 token accuracy delta, and semantic similarity (embedding cosine) deltas between FP32 baseline and quantized variant.
Cohort-stability score computed and documented; pass gate triggers if any cohort has stability score < 0.92 or top-1 accuracy drop > 1.5% relative to baseline.
Harness exposes results via JSON artifacts suitable for CI (s3 path or internal artifacts) and a summary webhook for the rollout orchestrator.
Integration test that simulates a failing quant profile and demonstrates rollout abort on gate failure.
Documentation page (Confluence) with usage, configuration knobs, and triage playbook is published.
tasks: Design cohort schema and canonical seed sets
Implement synthetic perturbation generator (typos, numeric perturbations, truncation, injected prompts)
Hook into calibration runner to replay KV cache-aware requests
Compute and persist per-request metrics and cohort aggregates
Implement pass/fail gate service and CI integration
Add console summary card and alert integration (PagerDuty threshold mapping)
Write integration tests and run end-to-end validation against an INT8 and FP8 profile
test_plan: Run harness against model-m-13b baseline (FP32) and two quant profiles (INT8-symmetric, FP8-e4m3). For each profile: generate cohorts, execute 2k replayed requests keeping KV states where applicable, collect metrics. Run bootstrapped statistical test for top-1 drop and semantic similarity. Validate gate behavior with controlled perturbation (introduce a synthetic adversarial cohort with paraphrase blockers). Record artifacts to s3://redwood-quant-tests/ENG-557890/{run_ts}/ and attach to CI job. Manual triage: if gate fails, attach diff examples and suggested fallback (model variant id, increase calibration steps, enable per-layer FP32 bypass).
metrics: cohort_stability_score: composite score [0..1] combining top-1 retention, perplexity ratio, and embedding cosine
top1_drop_pct: percentage point drop in most-likely token
failure_rate_on_adversarial_cohort: fraction of prompts where model output differs in critical token(s)
design_decisions: Use small deterministic seeds per cohort to make CI reproducible (randomness kept at driver level with fixed RNG seeds)
Compute metrics offline in a batch job to avoid perturbing serving cluster; replay uses local benchmarking cluster with the same kernel selection as production
Cohort-stability score favors semantic embedding similarity over raw token match for tasks that are generative and paraphrase-tolerant
Pass/fail thresholds conservative initially (low false-positive rate) and exposed as config to rollout policies
tradeoffs: Running full KV-aware replays increases fidelity but requires more infra and longer run times — initial rollout will sample 25% KV-corpus to balance time vs. signal
Embedding-based similarity can undercount critical token drops for arithmetic or code tasks; we therefore include top-1 and task-specific heuristics in cohorts
Conservative gates delay rollouts for marginal regressions; plan to add rollback-suggestion automation to speed mitigation
